stem: Two closed cylindrical storage tanks are similar. The ratio of the surface area of the smaller tank to the surface area of the larger tank is 9 to 16. The larger tank holds 128 cubic meters. How many cubic meters does the smaller tank hold?
explanation: For similar solids, the ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of lengths, so the length ratio is √(9/16) = 3/4.
The ratio of volumes is the cube of the length ratio: (3/4)³ = 27/64.
The smaller tank holds 128 × 27/64 = 54 cubic meters.
hints: If the area ratio is 9 : 16, what is the ratio of corresponding lengths?
